# PR Review Summary — #4353 [drawer] Add keyboard-aware drawer

**What it does:** Adds `Drawer.VirtualKeyboardProvider`, an opt-in component that adjusts a bottom-sheet drawer when a software keyboard opens — scroll-slack padding, centering the focused field in the visible visual viewport, and re-focusing tapped inputs without page scroll. +1647 / −110 across 16 files.

Branch `codex/drawer-ios-keyboard` was checked out and reviewed with 5 specialized agents (code, errors, tests, types, comments). `pnpm typescript` and `pnpm eslint` pass on the changed files.

## 🔴 Critical Issues (must resolve before merge)

**1. PR description contradicts the implementation** — *(code-reviewer, comment-analyzer)*
The GitHub description says it "Adds the `virtualKeyboardAware` prop" and "Removes `Drawer.VirtualKeyboardProvider`." The branch does the **opposite**: it adds the `Drawer.VirtualKeyboardProvider` component and there is no `virtualKeyboardAware` prop anywhere. Exports (`index.parts.ts:14`, `index.ts:17`), docs, and demos all consistently describe the provider — so the *code/docs/comments are internally consistent*, but the description (and any changelog tooling reading it) is stale or the wrong commits were pushed. Reconcile this — it's a question of which API the team actually wants to ship.

## 🟠 Important Issues (should address)

**2. Behavioral change to the existing (non-keyboard) swipe path** — *(code-reviewer)* `DrawerViewport.tsx:1064-1072`
`onTouchStart` now resolves `target` as `elementAtPoint ?? getTarget(nativeEvent)` instead of just `getTarget(nativeEvent)`. This `target` feeds the `contains()` guard and `findScrollableTouchTarget()` for **all** drawers, not just keyboard-aware ones, so swipe-vs-scroll arbitration can shift for existing users when `elementFromPoint` returns a different element than the event target. Scope it to the keyboard path, or justify it as a general improvement with a test for the non-keyboard case.

**3. Critical test gaps** — *(pr-test-analyzer)* Only 5 new tests (all Chromium-only) for a 534-line behavioral surface. Highest-value missing tests, in order:
- **Touchend re-focus of an *unfocused* input** (the headline iOS fix) — assert `focus()` called, `preventDefault()` called, and that `opacity`/`transform`/`transition` are **restored** by the `finally`. A regression here leaves an input at `translateY(-2000px)`/`opacity:0` — invisible. Only the *negative* (already-focused) case is tested today. `DrawerVirtualKeyboardProvider.tsx:472-487`
- **Restore on close/unmount** — only the blur restore path is covered; stale 288px padding on reopen would go uncaught. `overflowAnchor: 'none'` restoration is never asserted.
- **Nested-drawer suppression** + restore.
- **focusout → another input** element-switch path (`:91-94`).
- touchmove >10px tap-cancel boundary; hit-slop near-miss tap; label→control resolution; `prefers-reduced-motion` instant-scroll branch.

**4. Brittle test assertions** — *(pr-test-analyzer)* Exact-pixel literals like `paddingBottom).toBe('288px')` and `scrollTop).toBeCloseTo(270)` bake in three internal constants at once (`KEYBOARD_SCROLL_SLACK`, `KEYBOARD_VISIBILITY_MARGIN`, rect math). Tuning a constant breaks tests with an opaque "expected 288px." Prefer asserting the *contract* (input center lands within the visible viewport; padding ≥ base + slack).

## 🟡 Suggestions (nice to have)

- **Missing comments on non-obvious code** — *(comment-analyzer, code-reviewer)* The `translateY(-2000px)` focus hack (`:472`), the keyboard-detection heuristic in `getKeyboardVisualViewport` (`:517`), the hit-slop probe grid, and the `KEYBOARD_*`/`INPUT_TAP_*` magic numbers all warrant a one-line "why."
- **Reword docs prose** — *(comment-analyzer)* `page.mdx:49` "Existing drawers keep the legacy behavior" implies deprecation; the feature is purely opt-in. Say "drawers without this provider are unaffected."
- **Document the `onTouchEnd: boolean` contract** — *(type-design-analyzer)* The `true`-means-"handled, preventDefault called, skip swipe" contract lives only in the implementation. Add JSDoc on the context interface (`DrawerVirtualKeyboardContext.tsx:4`). (The void/boolean asymmetry itself is good design — keep it.)
- **`ScrollAdjustment` polish** — *(type-design-analyzer)* Mark fields `readonly`; the `paddingBottom` (inline string to restore) vs `computedPaddingBottom` (numeric baseline) naming is easy to confuse. Optionally name the `{ top, bottom }` return of `getKeyboardVisualViewport`.
- **Note the looser scroll-ancestor reimplementation** — *(code-reviewer)* `findPotentialScrollAncestor` (`:495`) intentionally omits the `scrollHeight > clientHeight` check that the shared `scrollable.ts` util enforces; a comment would satisfy the AGENTS.md "avoid duplicating logic" guideline.
- **`restoreKeyboardScrollAdjustment` theoretical leak** — *(silent-failure-hunter)* If a `style.*` write threw, `keyboardScrollAdjustmentRef` is never nulled (`:76-79`). Can't happen for real HTMLElements; a one-liner closes it. Borderline, non-blocking.

## ✅ Strengths

- **Clean error handling** — the `try/finally` style-restore is verified safe (restores even if `focus()` throws), `visualViewport` feature-detection degrades to a graceful no-op, and all listeners/rAFs are symmetrically cleaned up. No silent failures, no leaks.
- **Strong guideline compliance** — uses `useAnimationFrame`/`useStableCallback`, owner-safe `ownerDocument`/`ownerWindow`/`contains`/`getTarget`/`activeElement`, realm-safe `instanceof`, `-webkit-user-select` paired in demos, shared touch handlers via context (not duplicated). `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` passes.
- **Types follow repo conventions** — the empty `State {}` + `Props` + namespace triad is a faithful copy of `DrawerProvider`; correctly does *not* extend `BaseUIComponentProps` since it renders no element. Backward compatible (provider is optional via `?.`).
- **Docs/comments are accurate** vs the implementation, and the demo properly models header/footer-outside-scrollable-body.

## Recommended Action

1. **Resolve the description/implementation mismatch (#1)** — decide whether the shipped API is the provider or a prop.
2. **Clarify/scope the `onTouchStart` target change (#2)** and add a non-keyboard regression test.
3. **Fill the critical test gaps (#3)** — especially the unfocused-input re-focus + style-restore, and close/unmount restore.
4. **De-brittle assertions (#4)** and add the explanatory comments/JSDoc.
5. Re-run the review (and `code-simplifier`) after fixes.

## Pull request overview This PR adds an opt-in `Drawer.VirtualKeyboardProvider` to make bottom-sheet drawers behave better with software keyboards (notably iOS Safari), keeping the sheet frame stable and scrolling focused form fields into view while the keyboard is open. **Changes:** - Introduces `Drawer.VirtualKeyboardProvider`, including focus/visualViewport-driven keyboard inset + temporary scroll “slack” management. - Wires the provider into `Drawer.Viewport` touch handling so it can reliably distinguish taps vs drags even when swipe handling stops propagation. - Documents the new provider and the `--drawer-keyboard-inset` CSS variable, and adds demos/experiments showcasing recommended layouts. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 18 out of 18 changed files in this pull request and generated 1 comment.
